headline: Dallas taste is set in Oak Cliff, Deep Ellum and Fair Park. Win there first, then sell north.
thesis: Dallas fans resent being sold cowboy Texas. Their city is Fair Park's 1936 Texas Centennial buildings, Deep Ellum's layered walls and a Mexican-American Oak Cliff that sets taste long before Uptown or the suburbs catch on. The Mavs base is loyal but wounded: Dirk is sacred, the Luka trade is still raw and last season went 26-56. Cooper Flagg, under Masai Ujiri and Dusty May, is the first clean-slate reason to buy in two years. Football owns the fall and heat owns the summer, leaving 2026-27 a narrow window: opening week, four Cup group games, a possible December knockout run and the holiday gift peak. Sell product already in the pipeline now, and commission the Dallas-only capsules for 2027-28. Make them with paid, credited creators from Oak Cliff, Deep Ellum and Black South Dallas. Then send value-tiered volume to the Frisco, Allen and Grand Prairie doors, where most fans shop.

archetype.name: The Wounded Loyalists
archetype.description: A sprawling, multicultural metroplex crowd that still measures everything against Dirk and 2011. Guarded since the Luka trade, it will trust Flagg, and spend its kids' money on him, if the product feels like Dallas rather than generic Texas.

pulse.teamMoment: A full reset under new president Masai Ujiri and first-year coach Dusty May, built around Cooper Flagg. Kyrie Irving is back from his ACL tear, joined by Zaccharie Risacher, Santi Aldama and No. 9 pick Morez Johnson Jr. BetMGM sets the win total at 34.5, and the playoffs look unlikely.
pulse.sentiment: Cautious optimism. The 'Fire Nico' anger has burned out now that Harrison is gone and the Davis trade is done. Fans are still processing the Luka trade and a 26-56 season, and they'll reward visible development over hype.

topInsights.title: Dallas design starts at the 1936 Centennial
topInsights.insight: Locals file boots and ranches under Fort Worth and tourist Texas. The design language only Dallas owns is George Dahl's 1936 Texas Centennial Exposition at Fair Park: stepped pylons along the Esplanade, the Hall of State and buff-and-gold fairground lettering. That exposition was segregated. Its Hall of Negro Life, which displayed Aaron Douglas murals, was demolished soon after the fair closed, so the story only works if Black South Dallas tells it.
topInsights.implication: Build the Dallas graphic system on Centennial stepped geometry: Esplanade cream #E9DDBF and Centennial gold #C9A44C against Mavs navy, royal and silver. No neon red, no western cues. Develop it with the African American Museum, Dallas, inside Fair Park, as a paid advisory partner.

topInsights.title: Taste is set south and east, volume is bought north
topInsights.insight: Oak Cliff (Bishop Arts, Jefferson Boulevard, the Texas Theatre) and Deep Ellum decide what feels credible. Units move at Stonebriar, Grapevine Mills, Dick's and Academy. The arena store is a game-night ritual, not a volume door, and few suburban families ever visit the tastemaker doors.
topInsights.implication: Launch every Dallas-specific drop in Oak Cliff or Deep Ellum with the local creator there. Within days, send value-tiered versions to the northern suburbs. Outlets get prior-season product only.

topInsights.title: The Mexican-American core is the market, not a heritage night
topInsights.insight: Oak Cliff, West Dallas, Pleasant Grove, Irving, Garland and Grand Prairie hold a large, multigenerational, bilingual Mavs base. The team's 'Los Mavs' Noche Latina wordmark already sets the precedent. In the same neighborhoods, lowrider candy paint, pinstriping and hand-painted taqueria and storefront lettering are living crafts.
topInsights.implication: Once the team confirms the 2026-27 Noche Latina date, anchor a Spanish-first, Oak Cliff-made capsule on it, co-designed with paid, credited local painters. Treat Sept 16, Dia de Muertos, Nochebuena and Three Kings Day as community programming and gifting moments, not drops.

topInsights.title: Sell trust before triumph
topInsights.insight: Dirk's 41, his statue at American Airlines Center and the June 12, 2011 title over Miami are the only uncontested emotional ground. The Luka trade is an open wound, and a 34.5 win total makes 'new era' maximalism risky. Flagg is the one demand driver not tied to wins, and kids' demand skews to him.
topInsights.implication: Lead with understated, number-first Flagg youth and replica product, and make Dirk heritage an equal holiday line. Acknowledge the wound without naming it. Say plainly what the team is building (the gym, the kids, the city) in fans' own words: MFFL, Big D, 214. Test it with a local fan panel.

topInsights.title: The Mavs own an eight-week window between football and heat
topInsights.insight: Cowboys Sundays, Friday-night high school football, the State Fair and Red River weekend own the fall until mid-October. Triple-digit summers empty July and August. Dallas isn't on the Oct 20 opening-night slate or the Christmas slate. Its stage is its own opening week and four West Group A Cup games. Dallas hosts Houston on Oct 30 and Utah on Nov 6, then plays at Denver on Nov 24 and at Phoenix on Nov 27. A knockout run would need a top seed to bring a Dec 8-9 semifinal home.
topInsights.implication: Concentrate 2026-27 team product from opening week through the holiday peak. Tie any Cup product to the two home dates, Oct 30 and Nov 6, not a weekly cadence. Give the summer to the Dallas Wings instead of forcing Mavs product into the dead months.

topInsights.title: Heat, gym culture and the $100 tax-free line set the assortment
topInsights.insight: Texas's August sales tax holiday exempts clothing and footwear under $100 per item, just as DFW schools restart. Dallas barely has a coat season, and only a blue norther or ice storm makes people layer. Its hoopers play in church gyms, rec centers and Southern Dallas County fieldhouses, not on one famous outdoor court.
topInsights.implication: Target a $99.99 ceiling, pending Nike costing, for tees, shorts, mesh shooting shirts and youth product. Weight the range to mesh and light shells. Keep fleece to a thin November-February quarter-zip window.

topInsights.title: Southern Dallas County is the hoops story that survives any roster move
topInsights.insight: Duncanville, DeSoto, Lancaster, Skyline and Kimball form the talent belt every DFW program measures itself against. The same belt is home to a large Black fan base with deep high school, AAU and church-league ties.
topInsights.implication: A small 'Made in the Metroplex' gym pilot, with district sign-off and paid community partners, could give Nike a grassroots Dallas story that doesn't depend on the Mavs' record.

opportunities.title: Big D Heritage (Dirk 41 and the green eras)
opportunities.summary: Dirk is the safest emotional bet in the market. Sell Dirk heritage next to Flagg for the 2026 holiday run, then launch a new green-era line in 2027 on licenses started now.

opportunities.how: For 2026, box existing licensed Dirk product with a Flagg tee as a gift set. Start the Dirk likeness and 41 talks with his camp and the team now. Before choosing an era, test two looks with fans: the 1980s Blackman-Aguirre-Harper green and the mid-1990s Triple J (Jim Jackson, Jamal Mashburn, Jason Kidd). The original hat-and-M logo is team heritage and fine here, unlike new cowboy cues.

collection.name: Big D, Rebuilt (2027-28 build)
collection.story: A Dallas-only collection for a franchise starting over. It draws on the 1936 Centennial city of Fair Park, the layered walls of Deep Ellum and Oak Cliff's candy paint and hand lettering. Each is made with the local artists and institutions that own those languages. Mavs royal, navy and silver stay the anchor, and new color arrives as accents so it still reads as the team.

uniform.concept: Centennial: a 2028-29 City Edition pitch. For 2026-27, build around the current City Edition.
uniform.narrative: This season's job is to confirm Dallas's 2026-27 City Edition story and build the capsule, content and retail plan around it. For a future cycle, Centennial puts the 1936 Fair Park exposition on court, for a city done being reduced to boots and longhorns. It's developed with the African American Museum, Dallas, so the Hall of Negro Life is part of the story. City Edition themes are team-owned and NBA-reviewed, so the pitch goes to the Mavs and the league only after the partners agree.
motifs: Stepped pylon borders on the neck and armholes, drawn fresh rather than copied from any single building relief
Sunburst side panels in tonal navy jacquard
A thin gold inline on numbers and wordmark in the manner of 1936 fairground lettering
Area codes 214, 972 and 469 as a quiet hem or neck-tape detail
uniform.typography: A tall geometric 'DALLAS' wordmark and stepped numerals commissioned from a Black Dallas letterer, cream with a gold inline; no italic sports script and no star.
details: Waistband: repeating stepped-sunburst jacquard in navy on navy
Jock tag: 'BIG D 1936' in a stepped frame
Inner hang tag and launch content on the Hall of Negro Life, worded by the museum's advisors
Court: cream stepped baseline borders and a navy apron with a gold sideline pinline
avoid: Cowboy hats, boots, longhorns, rope or the Lone Star as a new hero mark. Dallas fans read them as Fort Worth or tourist Texas, and they crowd into Cowboys territory.
Fair Park nostalgia that skips the exposition's segregation, and the Tejas Warrior or any Indigenous figure from the Hall of State
A literal Pegasus, Big Tex, State Fair, Reunion Tower or Aaron Douglas mural imagery without licensing from the rights holders
Any reference to Luka Doncic, the 2025 trade or the previous front office
Repeating a concept from a past Mavs City Edition. Pull the full history with the team first.

risks.risk: Tone. Anything that reads as a victory lap, erases Luka or celebrates the old regime reopens the wound in a 34.5-win season. Total silence can read as evasive.
risks.mitigation: Speak plainly about the gym, the kids and the city in fans' own words, reviewed by a local fan panel. Never name Luka or Harrison, and avoid 'new era' framing.

risks.risk: Nike's player-footwear lever is weak. Flagg signed with New Balance and Irving's signature line is with Anta, so a Flagg or Kyrie sneaker hook is off the table.
risks.mitigation: Build Dallas on jerseys, apparel, Nike By You customization and a 2027-28 artist footwear collaboration. In content, feature only athletes with confirmed Nike ties.

risks.risk: Cultural extraction. Fair Park's segregated history, lowrider culture, Dia de Muertos, Juneteenth, the Dougie and Deep Ellum blues are community histories, and they backfire if borrowed.
risks.mitigation: Make Black South Dallas and Oak Cliff partners paid leads on flat up-front fees. Keep ceremonial imagery off product, and drop any framing the partners decline.

risks.risk: Rights. City Edition themes are team-owned and NBA-reviewed, and Cup marks belong to the league and sponsor. Quick-turn tees may sit with Fanatics. The Pegasus, Big Tex, State Fair, school marks, Aaron Douglas murals and Dirk's likeness each have separate owners.
risks.mitigation: Clear the Nike-versus-Fanatics split and Cup rights before any Cup product. Use original lettering and abstract forms by default, and start the Dirk license now.

risks.risk: Doors and timing come from model knowledge. The City Edition, home schedule, Noche Latina date, venues and festival dates are unverified, and capsule lead times push new product to 2027-28.
risks.mitigation: Run the verify list before committing. Limit 2026-27 to in-line product, merchandising, commissions and events.

scorecard.rationale: A huge, majority-minority metro with distinct design languages (the Fair Park Centennial, Deep Ellum, Oak Cliff) and a fresh Flagg reason to buy. Holding it back: football's grip on the fall, a car-bound retail map, a wounded fan base coming off 26-56 and partners not yet confirmed.
